    AI Overview
    The NASA Artemis rocket, known as the Space Launch System (SLS), stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall when fully stacked with the Orion crew capsule. It is taller than the Statue of Liberty and serves as the primary, super-heavy-lift vehicle designed for deep space missions, including the Artemis II lunar flyby. 
    • Height: 322 feet (
      ).
    • Comparison: Shorter than the 363-foot Apollo-era Saturn V, but taller than the 184-foot Space Shuttle.
    • Components: Consists of a 212-foot core stage with two 177-foot solid rocket boosters
      .
    • Mission: Launches the Orion capsule and crew to the Moon. 
    The SLS is designed as a super-heavy-lift vehicle to return humans to deep space. The rocket's massive size is necessary to deliver the power needed to send astronauts beyond Earth's orbit.

    How tall is the tallest rocket in the world?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    SpaceX's Starship is the tallest rocket ever built, standing approximately 120–123 meters (394–403 feet) tall when fully stacked. It consists of the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage, surpassing the height of the historic 111-meter (363-foot) Saturn V rocket. 
    Key Details on the Tallest Rockets: 
    • SpaceX Starship (120-123m): The current tallest and most powerful rocket ever constructed.
    • Saturn V (111m): The tallest rocket to have flown to the moon (NASA).
    • N1 Rocket (105m): The Soviet Union's counterpart to the Saturn V.
    • Space Launch System (SLS) (98m): NASA's Artemis moon rocket. 
    Starship's height allows it to carry a significantly larger payload than any previous rocket.
